cards.text: Friend, this one is about Abraham, the man God promised to make into a great nation (Genesis 12:2), and his wife Sarah. Sarah lives to be 127 years old. Then she dies in Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan.

cards.question: When Sarah dies in Hebron, what does her husband Abraham do?

answers.text: He goes out to mourn and weep for her
He leaves the land of Canaan for good
He sends word to his son Isaac

cards.text: Then Abraham gets up from beside his dead wife and speaks to the Hittites, the people living in that land. I think getting up from beside her is the hardest part.

cards.question: Sarah has died, and Abraham calls himself a foreigner and an outsider among the Hittites. He asks them to give him a ___ site among them.

cards.text: Abraham just called himself an outsider, and the Hittites answer him, “Listen to us, sir. You are God’s chosen one among us.” That's like introducing yourself as the new guy at work and finding out the whole office already knows your NAME.

cards.question: Abraham asks the Hittites for a burial site. They tell him that not one of them will hold back his tomb from him.
The Hittites call Abraham God's chosen one and tell him to bury Sarah in the finest of their tombs. What does Abraham do next?

answers.text: He rises and bows down before them
He turns down any help from them
He leaves to look for land elsewhere

cards.text: Abraham asks them to approach Ephron son of Zohar for him. He's got the exact spot picked out, friend: the cave of Machpelah at the end of Ephron's field, sold to him for full price right in front of everyone.
Abraham's asking the Hittites to go talk to Ephron for him. Ephron? He's sitting RIGHT THERE among them, with all the Hittites who came to the gate of his city listening.

cards.question: Abraham wants to buy the cave of Machpelah. With all the Hittites listening at the city gate, what does Ephron tell him about the cave?

answers.text: He gives it to Abraham as a gift
He offers a different cave instead

cards.text: Ephron's giving him the field AND the cave in it, right in front of his people. Again Abraham bows down before the people of the land, and the WHOLE city gate leans in like it's the last five seconds of a tied game.

cards.question: Ephron offers Abraham the field and the cave as a gift. Abraham still insists on paying Ephron the price of the field.

cards.text: Ephron says the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, then adds, “…what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.” Friend, I got sold for twenty-five cents at a bakery closing sale, and Ephron's out here talking about four hundred shekels like it's NOTHING.

cards.question: Ephron says the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver. Abraham weighs out ___ hundred shekels for him.

cards.text: Abraham weighs out the silver by the standard of the merchants. Ephron's field at Machpelah near Mamre and the cave in it are deeded over to him in front of all the Hittites at the gate of Ephron's city.

cards.question: Abraham buys Ephron's field at Machpelah. The trees growing within the field's boundaries stay with Ephron.
The field and the cave at Machpelah are now Abraham's. What does he do there?

answers.text: He buries his wife Sarah in the cave
He gives the field back to Ephron
He builds a city on the field

cards.text: The man who called himself a foreigner and an outsider now has a field and a cave in Canaan, deeded to him as a burial site. And friend, Abraham's story isn't finished yet.
